content:
Facts: Legitimate heirs sought reduction of a lifetime donation of land made by the deceased to two children with reservation of usufruct, alleging infringement of their reserved shares, and requested restitution in kind or monetary reinstatement.
Legal framework
Articles 542, 554–556, 561, 564, 737 and 555(2) of the Italian Civil Code on reserved shares, reduction of testamentary dispositions and donations, fictitious reconstitution, order of reduction, collation, and restitution; procedural rules on res judicata and court-appointed expert evidence.
Interpretative issue
Whether the reduction action concerning a donation exempted from collation is admissible and how the order and modalities of reduction and reinstatement of the reserved share must be determined when restitution in kind of the donated property is impracticable.

Principle applied
Reduction of testamentary dispositions and donations constitutes a single action protecting forced heirs, irrespective of collation exemptions. The assessment of infringement follows fictitious reconstitution at the opening of succession, valuing assets at that time and disregarding consolidated usufruct. Reduction must follow the statutory order under Article 555(2) ICC. Where restitution in kind of donated assets would cause excessive fragmentation and loss of value, reinstatement of the reserved share may occur partly through restitution in kind of remaining estate assets and partly through monetary compensation charged to the beneficiaries of the donation.
